title: The Battle of Hastings
description: October 1066. William of Normandy's invasion army faces King Harold's Anglo-Saxon shield wall on Senlac Hill. The player commands the Norman force and must break the shield wall through feigned retreats and combined cavalry-archer assaults before nightfall ends the battle.

anachronisms_found: 44 STONE_WALL segments, a GATE_NORTH_TO_SOUTH and 4 GUARD_TOWERs for the Anglo-Saxon player: Harold's army fought an open-field defensive action on the Senlac ridge with no fortifications whatsoever; the engine offered palisades or simply massed infantry, so a stone-walled fortress is an avoidable invention

TOWN_CENTER, MONASTERY, BLACKSMITH, STABLE and ARCHERY_RANGE for both sides turn a one-day field battle into a base-vs-base fight; neither army had installations at Senlac (William's only work was the prefab motte at Hastings, several miles off)
16 SKIRMISHERs in the Saxon roster: contemporary accounts (and the Bayeux Tapestry) show the English fielding essentially no missile troops at Hastings — that was the Norman advantage
Anglo-Saxon STABLE building implies mounted forces; Harold's housecarls dismounted to fight and the shield wall was entirely on foot
4174 TREE_OAK tiles render Senlac as dense forest; the ridge itself was open ground with the Andredsweald at the Saxon rear only

issues_found: Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so the architecture set and unit bonuses are unpredictable — Britons/Franks (or Byzantines for Norman knights) were available and would have fixed Anglo-Saxon and Norman visual identity.

Harold Godwinson is represented by the generic KING unit, a non-combat, near-defenceless piece; the man who reportedly fought on foot in the shield wall until struck down is thus a passive object rather than a fighting champion-class stand-in.

Player 2 holds 44 STONE_WALL segments, a GATE and 4 GUARD_TOWERs. Harold's army fought on an unfortified ridge with no masonry whatsoever; the shield wall as stone curtain plus towers turns Senlac Hill into a castle-town siege.

4,174 oak trees smother a 120x120 map; the ridge above the Hastings marsh was open downland with the Andredsweald behind, not near-continuous forest, and heavy woods make the cavalry envelopment the brief promises impossible to stage.
Both sides have TOWN_CENTER, MILL, HOUSE, MONASTERY, BARRACKS, STABLE, ARCHERY_RANGE etc. — a settled economy neither invasion army nor the hastily assembled Saxon host possessed on the field.

16 SKIRMISHERs on the Saxon side overstates Anglo-Saxon missile troops, whose near-absence at Hastings was a decisive weakness; the Normans' archer arm (10 ARCHER vs 21 KNIGHT) is correspondingly underweighted.

Secondary victory VC2 awards the Norman player the battle simply for having a unit alive after 600 seconds — the nightfall deadline historically favoured Harold, whose army only had to hold until dark, so this inverts the clock.
Defeat on loss of the player's TOWN_CENTER is a generic AoE2 condition with no counterpart at Hastings; the Normans had no base to lose beyond the Pevensey/Hastings camp, which was never threatened.

The signature feigned retreats are only narrated in text; no trigger (PATROL/TASK_OBJECT) models a Norman withdrawal drawing the fyrd off the ridge, so the player never performs the tactic the brief centres on.
Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so Norman and Anglo-Saxon architecture and unit bonuses are left to chance (Franks/Britons were the obvious, available choices).

Player 2 (the Saxons) is given 44 STONE_WALL segments, a GATE_NORTH_TO_SOUTH and 4 GUARD_TOWERs. Harold's army fought a field battle behind a shield wall of men on an open ridge; there were no fortifications at Senlac, and the walls flatly contradict the scenario's own narration about breaking a shield wall.

4,174 TREE_OAK objects dominate a 120x120 map; the Hastings battlefield was an open slope with marshy ground below the ridge, not dense forest, and heavy woods make cavalry envelopment and the feigned-retreat pursuit unrepresentable.

Both sides own TOWN_CENTER, STABLE, ARCHERY_RANGE, BLACKSMITH and MONASTERY - base furniture for a one-day pitched battle where neither army had a settlement; a Norman TOWN_CENTER loss is even wired as a defeat condition, an event with no historical counterpart.
The Saxon force includes 16 SKIRMISHERs; Harold's army was notably short of missile troops, and this over-arms the shield wall with skirmishers while the Normans get only 10 archers.
Secondary victory 'VC2' awards the win merely for having one unit alive anywhere on the map at 600 seconds, so a passive player can win without ever engaging the shield wall.

Dialogue line 'The Duke has fallen! Normandy's cause dies with him!' fires on William's death - a counterfactual outcome presented without flagging that William in fact survived (only rumours of his death circulated).
